newsitem.title: GERMANY: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.
newsitem.headline: F.O. LICHT - Daily sugar report.

text.p: The following is a direct contribution from statistician F.O. Licht in Ratzeburg, Germany. Please address any queries to Helmut Ahlfeld on +00 49 4541 88920.

White sugar futures in London ended mixed in quiet trade aided by some short-covering ahead of the Christmas/New Year holidays. Little activity is expected next week but the recent bearish sentiment is likely to persist due to abundant supply of quality whites. March ended $1.50 higher at $305.10 per tonne, while May added $1.90 to close at $305.10. By contrast, August gave up $2.1 to close at $305.60.

In New York sugar futures settled a thinly-traded session barely lower, as prices drifted on both sides of unchanged throughout the session. There was some short-covering and fund buying. Producers were steady scale-up sellers throughout the week, capping the market's attempt to rally to psychologically key 11.00 cents/lb. However, current slack enduser demand is likely to keep prices under pressure. March ended 2 points lower at 10.69 cents/lb, while May remained unchanged at 10.76 cents/lb.

CHINA - According to the Sugar Association, sugar production in 1996/97 (October/September) could reach 7.174 million tonnes, raw value, slightly above earlier estimates and up on last year's figure of 6.8 million tonnes. Of the total expected to be produced in 1996/97, 1.511 million tonnes (1.403 million tonnes) is expected to be beet and 5.663 million tonnes (5.367 million tonnes) cane sugar.

According to preliminary figures, China exported 25,521 tonnes of sugar, raw value, in November 1996, significantly down on the 92,450 tonnes exported the same month the previous year. That brought total exports since the beginning of 1996/97 (September) up to 163,000 tonnes, which compares to 189,300 tonnes exported the same period in 1995. Total exports in crop year 1995/96 (September/August) reached 830,200 tonnes, up from 540,000 tonnes exported in 1994/95 but down on the 1.102 million tonnes exported in 1993/94.

ZIMBABWE - Sugar production in Zimbabwe in 1996 will be lower than had been expected. While original estimates were for a total crop of 380,000 tonnes, raw value, the latest figure is not more than 336,000 tonnes up from 512,000 tonnes produced in 1995. Total production in 1997 is forecast to rebound strongly to 630,000 tonnes.

TURKEY - Turkish state sugar company Turkseker is planning to export 300,000 tonnes of sugar, white value, in calendar year 1997, mostly to Azerbaijan, Georgia and Uzbekistan, industry sources said. Total production in 1996/97 is expected to reach 1.850 million tonnes, white value, of which Turkseker will account for 1.500 million tonnes, while 350,000 tonnes are expected to be produced by the three private companies. Production in 1995/96 was 1.375 million tonnes of which Turkseker produced 1.100 million tonnes. Turkish officials said earlier Turkseker had offered to sell to Iraq 50,000 tonnes of sugar under the UN oil-for-food deal, which allows Bagdad to sell oil worth $2 billion over six months to buy food and medicine. It was added that Turkseker could also use output from its Karsamba refinery on the Black Sea which it turned to a refinery in 1995. Turkey imported about 100,000 tonnes of raws earlier in 1996, processed into whites at Karsamba. It exported 12,500 tonnes of the output from Karsamba through a tender in June and holds the remaining output in stocks.

ITALY - Sugar imports in July 1996 amounted to 29,518 tonnes, raw value, down from last year's 34,893 tonnes. This brought total imports in 1995/96 up to 379,026 tonnes, raw value, sharply up on last year's 266,279 tonnes and the 218,678 tonnes imported in 1993/94. Major countries of origin in 1995/96 for white sugar were France with 170,862 tonnes whites against 136,182 tonnes, Germany with 78,817 tonnes, up from 53,906 tonnes and the United Kingdom with 33,471 tonnes compared to 27,299 tonnes. Sugar exports in July 1996 amounted to 16,385 tonnes, up from last year's 2,596 tonnes. This brought total exports in 1995/96 up to 170,210 tonnes against 124,787 tonnes in 1994/95 and 182,179 tonnes in 1993/94. Major countries of destination in October/July 1995/96 were Turkey with 32,314 tonnes whites against 1,254 tonnes, Lebanon with 25,286 tonnes, hardly changed from last year's 25,165 tonnes and Slovenia with 19,606 tonnes compared to 16,891 tonnes.
